text:
jessica: customer on Dedicated (VPC) reporting intermittent 403s and TLS handshake failures when calling our hosted API from private app subnet. Works from their office/public internet. They say DNS resolves to the endpoint IP but requests sometimes fail with 'TLS alert' or 403. Escalating — any quick checks?

mira: can you grab a few things from the app host: `dig +short api.redwood.internal` (or whatever hostname they're using), `curl -v https://api.redwood.internal/health` and `openssl s_client -connect <IP>:443 -servername api.redwood.internal -tlsextdebug -status`? Also a `traceroute -n <IP>` and `tcpdump -i eth0 host <IP> and port 443` while running the curl.

jessica: got results from customer, pasted below. (they're on AWS private subnets)
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.internal
10.0.54.23

$ curl -v https://api.redwood.internal/health
* Connected to 10.0.54.23 (10.0.54.23) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake error: SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert handshake failure
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to 10.0.54.23:443

$ openssl s_client -connect 10.0.54.23:443 -servername api.redwood.internal
CONNECTED(00000003)
140123456789120:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure:../ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1398
---
No peer certificate available
---

$ traceroute -n 10.0.54.23
 1 10.0.1.1 0.123 ms 0.073 ms 0.053 ms
 2 10.0.54.23 0.234 ms 0.182 ms 0.161 ms
```

jessica: tcpdump shows SYN, SYN-ACK, then client sends FIN immediately (weird).

tony: a few possibilities in this pattern:
- endpoint SG might be restrictive (interface endpoints have ENIs in subnets; SG must allow client source ports). Check the endpoint SG inbound allows ephemeral ports from the app subnet and outbound allows 443 to our side.
- VPC endpoint policy could be rejecting the call if the principal/conditions don't match (less common for TLS handshake failures but worth checking).
- DNS split-horizon or stale host entries: if the app sometimes resolves to our public IP (or they have an /etc/hosts entry pointing to a public IP), traffic could be routed via NAT/Egress and then blocked by the customer's external allowlist, causing handshake failures or 403s.
- An inline proxy or egress gateway (NAT GW, firewall) could be intercepting TLS (MITM) and failing SNI/cert validation.

mira: also validate the SNI value — we require clients to use the api hostname in SNI. If the client is doing IP-based SSL (no SNI), our cert won't match and handshake fails. Ask them to run the openssl command with `-servername` (they already did but confirm their app sends SNI).

jessica: customer sent app logs showing the app sometimes falls back to an IP literal hostname resolution in code path and does `curl https://10.0.54.23/…` (no SNI). Example log: `calling https://10.0.54.23/health` — that would break cert validation.

mira: that explains the TLS handshake failures. Why would it resolve to 10.0.54.23 sometimes and something else other times? Two more checks: `getent hosts api.redwood.internal` (to see NSS order), and `cat /etc/hosts` on the app hosts. Also verify resolver (are they using custom dns forwarding or Route 53 inbound endpoints?).

jessica: they ran `cat /etc/hosts` and found a leftover line mapping api.redwood.internal -> 3.120.45.12 (their old staging workaround). They removed it and retried.

infra-bot: infra change yesterday 2025-08-02T17:02Z: updated outbound IP allowlist for edge egress; removed 3.120.45.12 from allowed list (policy id: allowlist-987).

oncall-luis: that combination explains the 403s when the host was using the public IP: traffic went out via NAT/EGRESS and hit our public edge, which then refused or returned 403 because the request came from unknown client IP (or because that IP was delisted). When they hit the interface endpoint IP with SNI everything should work — but their app switched to IP literal sometimes, causing cert/SNI problems and then fallback to public path created the 403.

tony: remedial checklist we recommended to customer:
- remove stale /etc/hosts entries (done).
- ensure app uses hostname (SNI) not bare IP; add a test `openssl s_client -connect 10.0.54.23:443 -servername api.redwood.internal` and compare cert CN/SAN.
- confirm endpoint SG allows inbound from app subnet ephemeral ports and outbound to 443. Example SG inbound: `tcp 443 source 10.0.0.0/16`, outbound: `tcp ephemeral to 0.0.0.0/0` (or tighten to our endpoint if you have static egress).
- if using egress allowlist on their side, add our current public edge IP range as a fallback (we provided the range) and keep it in sync via our published list.
- check for proxy env vars (HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY) that might force public egress.

jessica: customer removed hosts entry and redeployed app. They ran the curl and now get 200 OK over TLS: `* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Finished` `HTTP/2 200`

mira: root cause: stale /etc/hosts pointing to public IP + app code path that sometimes uses IP literal (no SNI) -> handshake failures; some requests went via public egress and failed due to our allowlist change causing 403s.

mira: action items:
- we will send KB to customer summarizing the fix and commands to validate (dig/getent/openssl).
- infra: publish a clear note on allowed public IPs and change window.
- docs: add a short Troubleshooting guide for PrivateLink/interface endpoints (SNI, /etc/hosts, SG, egress allowlist).

jessica: customer confirmed fixed and will monitor. Closing the escalation after a 24h watch. :thumbsup:
